reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: Measured barnacle removal stresses follow the sqrt(E/t) trend only roughly (viscoelastic dissipation, cupping and embedding on very soft silicones), and part of the compliance is lost to the stiff graded base, so about 30 % lower release stress than a good commercial foul-release topcoat is realistic rather than 50 %. Merchant ships at 12-16 kn already shed most macrofouling from commercial foul-release coatings; the benefit appears mainly after idle periods, while slime, the dominant in-service penalty, is not affected, so about 1 % of time-averaged friction.
key_assumption_issues: Kendall/Brady energy scaling with an elastic work of adhesion of 0.05 J/m^2; real barnacle cement adhesion involves viscoelastic dissipation and does not scale cleanly
Exponential modulus profile across the full 400 um thickness; the actual profile of a nass-in-nass sprayed system is uncertain and sets the compliance loss
The model gives release stress of a rigid disc, not the hydrodynamic load actually available on a fouler at a given ship speed
Auto-filled parameters d2u_dxi2=1 and du_dxi=1 appear in the audited list (pipeline artefact, not used physically)
killer_risks: Ultra-soft top layer (tear strength ~0.5-1 kN/m) is cut by fenders, chains, debris and in-water cleaning; damaged spots foul and roughen, erasing the benefit within 1-2 years
Slime is untouched by softness, so the dominant in-service drag penalty of foul-release coatings remains
Low-crosslink PDMS may contain unreacted oligomers that leach

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The 67 % comes from lab adhesion strengths of fresh amphiphilic surfaces (12 vs 30 Pa) put into an exponential survival law; after months in service and with 10-40 % idle time at zero shear, the reduction of retained slime is more like 20 %. Since slime adds perhaps 5 % to time-averaged friction on foul-release ships, 20 % less slime gives about 1 %.
key_assumption_issues: The adhesion-strength ratio 12 vs 30 Pa is a free input from short-term lab data and fully determines the gain
Exponential survival exp(-tau_w/tau_adh) is assumed, not derived
Constant service wall shear of 25 Pa ignores idle periods where the benefit vanishes and the biofilm consolidates
Settlement flux is a proxy for slime thickness; biofilm growth after attachment is not modelled
killer_risks: Zwitterionic surface segments are buried by silicone surface reconstruction, fouled by conditioning films and oil, and abraded within months
Hydrogel swelling weakens the matrix and adhesion to the tie layer
Consolidated slime from idle periods is not removed later at service shear

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: No conventional baseline was simulated, and the metric (surface confinement of hydrolysis) says nothing about fouling. Biocide-free eroding coatings foul with barnacles and weed within months because um-per-month erosion cannot dislodge settled larvae, whereas silicone foul-release at least sheds macrofouling at speed, so the time-averaged drag is likely a few percent worse than the baseline.
reviews.baseline_issue: No baseline was simulated; the silicone foul-release baseline has no counterpart in this metric.
key_assumption_issues: Water diffusivity and hydrolysis constant were changed by two orders of magnitude by the auditor to obtain surface confinement; the proposed values gave bulk hydrolysis within weeks
The erosion rate is not predicted by the model (the front estimate is 500 times too fast); removal by flow and ion exchange is missing
No link from erosion to fouling removal is modelled
killer_risks: Without a biocide, surface erosion of a few um per month does not remove settled barnacle cyprids or tubeworms; the hull fouls
About 0.36 kg/m^2 of polymer fragments released into the sea over five years (microplastic unless fully biodegradable)
Erosion rate strongly depends on temperature and speed; reservoir exhausted before docking in warm waters
